Flow: Fulfilling a customer's order

Stages, and where each is measured exists proposed cannot be counted

The case, whom it serves, what it delivers

One case
One order
Starts
The order's record is written in Submitted
Ends
The customer has the goods
Serves
  • The customer who placed the order expects the customer has the goods, or is told definitively that the order will not be filled (proposed).

    Met when:

    • The order delivered to the customer, or Cancelled with its reason (lack of stock, a failed payment or the customer's request).
    • The code's last recorded state is Shipped (proposed).
Delivers
  • Fulfil customer orders
  • Take and process customer orders
  • Notify outside parties of business events

How many checkouts reaching Ordering API ended without their order being written?
Kind

cases
Counted how

ordering-api log over the window, by request id:

  • Those with a 'Sending command:' line for the create command (Ordering.API/Apis/OrdersApi.cs:148-153) and no 'CreateOrderCommand succeeded - RequestId:' line (:159), that is the 'CreateOrderCommand failed - RequestId:' lines (:163) and the requests that threw before answering.
  • Against all such request ids.

A retried call carries the same request id and counts once.

Was each of this order's lines written at the catalogue price in force when it was placed?
Kind
failure rate
Counted on
cases
Counted how

per order, each ordering.orderItems "UnitPrice" against catalog "Price" at the order's "OrderDate": the current price, unwound through the ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent rows in catalogdb's "IntegrationEventLog" ("Content" holds the old and new price, "CreationTime" when) written after it.

A line for a product no longer in the catalogue counts too.

Whether the lines match the basket cannot be checked: the basket is deleted (WebApp/Services/BasketState.cs:107-108).
